description: Machine-readable LazyBooks data model. Dexie stores, SQLite DDL, the Tally wire mapping and the fixtures all derive from this file.

amounts.wire: JSON string matching ^-?\d+(\.\d{1,4})?$ ; canonical form = at least 2 and at most 4 decimals, trailing zeros beyond the 2nd removed (examples: '1180.00', '0.50', '12.3456')
amounts.storage: INTEGER = value x 10^4 (scale 4) for every decimal column, in both Dexie and SQLite; sums are integer sums
amounts.rounding: half away from zero when a source has more than 4 decimals; tax and totals use currency decimals (tm_company.decimal_places, default 2) with half away from zero
amounts.sign: ledger amounts keep the Tally sign: debit negative, credit positive. Quantities are stored positive; direction comes from the voucher kind and is_deemed_positive
amounts.safe_range: JS numbers are exact up to 2^53-1 minor units (about 900 billion currency units); aggregate sums that could exceed it must use BigInt in the Dexie adapter; SQLite uses 64-bit integers

dates.datetimes: ISO-8601 UTC with Z (only in control/queue data, not in tm_/tx_ tables)

booleans.storage: integer 0|1 in both adapters (IndexedDB cannot key booleans)

conventions.nulls: No column used by an index or primary key may be null. Text columns are never null (empty string = none). Only date and json columns may be null.
conventions.guid: Use the GUID Tally gives. When Tally gives none (some godowns, cost centres, employees) use 'n:' + exact name. A guid is never recomputed once stored.
conventions.names_vs_guids: Tally exports many references by NAME. Every reference column pair is <thing>_name (as given) and <thing>_guid (resolved by the connector through the shared resolver; empty string when unresolved). Devices must prefer the guid and fall back to the name.
conventions.company_scope: Every table except tm_company and ref_voucher_kind has company_guid as the first primary-key column and as the first column of every index.
conventions.json_columns: JSON values round-trip as objects in Dexie and as TEXT in SQLite
conventions.alter_id: Tally AlterID of the object. Masters carry alter_id; vouchers carry alter_id and master_id. Incremental pulls use alter_id > last seen max (TALLY_WIRE section 4).
conventions.verify_values: legacy_seen = the tag appears in the legacy connector field lists (behaviour reference only); assumed = standard Tally tag from public documentation, verify on a real Tally; derived = computed by the connector, no Tally tag

ref_voucher_kind.description: Static seed shipped with every app and with the vault; never synced in v1. Company-defined voucher types resolve to one of these via tm_voucher_type.base_kind.

columns.name: tally_name

columns.name: party_side

columns.name: entry_kind
columns.derive: entry_queue kind that creates this base kind; empty = not creatable in v1

device_tables.description: Tables that exist only on a device or only in the license project; defined elsewhere.
device_tables.license_project: See sql/02_license_project_schema.sql: followups, reminder_jobs, reminder_log, punch_logs, team_users, app_settings (mirrored on the device where useful); devices, sync_requests, sync_chunks, entry_queue, snapshots are transient and never mirrored
